The leads give a Jericho headcount in the return lists, a bare 'Zachor', or other men named Zakchour with different fathers; none ties these wall-builders to another notice beyond the city name or a recurring personal name.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The men of Jericho and Zakchour son of Amari are not equated with return-register households solely from a city or recurring name; no securely matching individual notice is retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names Iedaia son of Eromaph repairing opposite his house and Atous son of Asbania. The leads show other repairers working opposite their own houses or a bare 'Atous' in a list of names; they share only the general practice or a name without a matching father.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The individual repairers and location opposite a house do not establish a sufficiently precise cross-reference merely through shared names or the general practice of repairing nearby walls.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names the Levite Raoum son of Bani and Asabia, ruler of half the district of Keila. The leads give other half-district rulers of different districts, a 'Keilam' in a town list, Levite supervisors in general, or an Asabia who is the father of Ozi; none identifies these men or Asabia's office.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Raoum son of Bani and Asabia's district office are not identified with similarly named figures in other lists without firmer genealogical evidence.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names Azour son of Iesous, ruler of Masphe, repairing at the tower of the ascent by the corner. The leads give Uzziah's corner towers, Levites named Jesus or Jesou, or other second sections; none matches Azour, Masphe or this tower.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Azour son of Iesous at Masphe is not linked to the high priest or other Iesous figures from a shared patronymic alone.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names only priests called men of Achechar repairing the wall; no shown text uses the designation Achechar, and the other passages merely share a gathering or a generic verb of repairing, so no specific group can be matched.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The priests called men of Achechar have no verified matching group in the passages selected for this review; the designation is not replaced from another edition.

closed_source_units.reason: Benjamin, Asoub and Azaria son of Maasea son of Anania appear only as builders opposite or beside their houses; other uses of Asoub, Azaria or Anania carry different fathers or no identifying detail, and the remaining texts are other builders in the same wall list or unrelated assemblies.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The adjacent households of Benjamin, Asoub and Azaria are particular boundary notices without a securely identified external counterpart.

closed_source_units.reason: Saddouk son of Emmer and Samaia son of Sechenia, keeper of the East Gate, are wall builders; the Emmer census totals and the Samaia son of Sechenia of a royal genealogy share only names, with no gatekeeping or building role to show the same persons, and the remaining texts concern unrelated gates.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Saddouk son of Emmer and Samaia son of Sechenia are not attached to priestly or other return-register families merely from recurring names.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit lists Anania son of Selemia, Anoum and Mesoulam son of Barchia repairing sections; the only other texts are different builders in the same wall list sharing the phrase 'second section', which identifies no person or event.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The name forms, paternal chains and second-section notice are kept as printed; an exact identity with another Mesoulam or Anania is not established solely through resemblance.

closed_source_units.reason: Melchia son of Saraphi, Bethanathinim and the gate of Maphekad appear nowhere else; the other Melchia/Melchias builders have different fathers, and the adjacent notice of dealers in small wares only continues the same wall list without identifying these sites.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Melchia son of Saraphi, Bethanathinim and Maphekad are not given an unverified identity or mapped onto a differently named gate.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is Judah's complaint about rubble and inability to build the wall; the other texts share only generic statements of inability, labour or building in unrelated settings (the spies' report, Solomon's workforce, Haggai's delay), none of which matches this complaint.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The supplied text says the strength of the enemies has been crushed, rather than importing a familiar reading about exhausted builders; no sufficiently precise connection is retained for this unusual statement.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit reports that Nehemiah and the guard never took off their clothes; the other texts concern labour, leadership, garments or nakedness in unrelated situations and contain no matching practice of constant readiness.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Not taking off clothes is a specific readiness practice here; an unrelated journey or garment instruction does not establish the same action or purpose.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is Nehemiah's grief at the outcry over debt; the other texts share only a general expression of grief or anger (Moses, Jesus, the Psalms, Nehemiah's later reforms) with no common cause or event.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The narrator's deep grief introduces the response to the outcry, but a generic anger or grief reaction does not supply a particular independent target.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit describes 150 Jews and visitors from the nations at Nehemiah's table; the other texts mention eating at a king's or queen's table or general hospitality, with no matching company, number or occasion.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The 150 guests and visitors from surrounding nations have no matching numbered company or independently described meal established here.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit only says the same message came again and was answered likewise; none of the other texts concerns this exchange, and their shared ideas of persistence or reporting accordingly are generic.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The repeated message and reply have no additional independent target; the supplied unit is not expanded with a familiar number of repetitions absent from its wording.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is Nehemiah's refusal to enter the house to save his life; the other texts share only general courage or the verb 'live' in unrelated settings, and none addresses entering the house.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The short question about who could enter the house and live may invite comparison with sanctuary-access law, but the supplied wording does not establish the precise sacred area or priestly status needed to resolve that application; the candidate remains zero credit.

closed_source_units.reason: Iram, Meramoth and Abdia are listed only as names among the sealing priests; the Meramoth son of Ouria son of Akos who builds the wall and the various Abdias are not shown to be priests of this list, and the other texts are unrelated names.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Iram, Meramoth and Abdia are not assigned identities in another priestly list or delivery account merely from similar names.

closed_source_units.reason: Sabania, Odouia, Kalita, Pheleia and Anan are bare Levite names; Kalita only resembles the Levite Kolia/Kolitas, and the other texts list different Levites or unrelated people named Odouia, so no individual can be matched.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Sabania, Odouia, Kalita, Pheleia and Anan are not assigned other identities; Kalita's resemblance to Kolia/Kolitas in the separately read candidate does not establish that individual identification.

closed_source_units.reason: Micha, Roob and Esebias are bare Levite names; the Asabia/Asebia and Micha of other lists differ in form or appear in different genealogies, and Roob elsewhere is a place, so no specific identification exists.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Micha, Roob and Esebias have no distinguishing ancestry or action here that establishes a particular comparison with other named people.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit reads only 'Odouia, sons of Banounai'; the other Odouia/Odouias texts belong to unrelated genealogies or a military division, and no list names the sons of Banounai.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The wording Odouia, sons of Banounai is preserved without reconstructing an ancestry to align it with another Levitical list.

closed_source_units.reason: Magaphes, Mesoulam and Ezir are bare names among the rulers; Mesoulam is a common name borne by several men with different fathers (son of Basodia, son of Barchia), and nothing in the unit shows which, if any, is meant.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Magaphes, Mesoulam and Ezir lack distinguishing patronymics or a separately verified event sufficient to identify them with other bearers.

closed_source_units.reason: Mesozebel, Saddouk and Jeddoua are bare names among the rulers; the various Saddouks elsewhere are a builder, a scribe and high-priestly ancestors with no detail linking any of them to this signatory.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Mesozebel, Saddouk and Jeddoua are preserved without equating the signatories with other similarly named priests, scribes or family heads.

closed_source_units.reason: Phaltia, Anan and Anaia are bare names; the other texts concern unrelated men named Anan in royal or tribal genealogies, so nothing identifies these signatories.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Phaltia, Anan and Anaia have no independently established identities outside this list; shared names alone are insufficient.

closed_source_units.reason: Osee, Anania and Asoub are bare names; the Asoubs and Ananias elsewhere have different fathers or roles (a builder son of Phaathmoab, a Levite's father, a royal deputy), so no identification is supported.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Osee, Anania and Asoub are not assigned the biographies or roles of other similarly named figures without further distinguishing evidence.

closed_source_units.reason: Aloes, Phalai and Sobek are personal names in the seal list; the only other text uses 'aloes' as a spice at Jesus' burial, which is unrelated.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Aloes, Phalai and Sobek are listed without additional identifying relationships sufficient for a particular retained comparison.

closed_source_units.reason: Raoum, Esabana and Maasaia are signatories among the rulers of the people; the Raoum of Ezra 4 is a Persian official opposing Jerusalem and the Raoum son of Bani is a Levite builder, neither matching this role.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Raoum, Esabana and Maasaia are not identified with officials, returnees or attendants elsewhere solely by names in this seal list.

closed_source_units.reason: Aia, Ainan and Enan are personal names in the seal list; the other texts use Ainan as a place name on Israel's northern border or near Timnah, which is unrelated.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Aia, Ainan and Enan remain the source's actual forms; no name normalization or speculative personal identification supplies a retained link.

closed_source_units.reason: Malouch, Eram and Baana close the rulers' list as bare names; the other Malouch texts are the priestly Malouch of the priest lists or a son of Banoui in Ezra, not shown to be this ruler.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Malouch, Eram and Baana close the list without specifying that they are particular earlier individuals or entire named returnee families.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit gives 468 men of ability among the sons of Phares in Jerusalem; the other texts share only numbers or the word 'ability' in unrelated contexts, and no shown passage records this group.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The 468 men of the Phares group are not equated with the different family and count of Zara's descendants in Chronicles; no verified matching enumeration is retained.

closed_source_units.reason: Joel son of Zechri and Joudas son of Asana are overseers of the Benjaminites in Jerusalem; the other texts name different Joels, a Benjaminite Salo, or the sons of Asana building a gate, none showing these men or their office.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Joel son of Zechri and Joudas son of Asana have no securely identified matching overseer notice in the compared Jerusalem register.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit gives 242 heads of families and Amessai son of Esdriel; the other texts name an unrelated Esdriel among Transjordan chiefs or speak of 'families of the nations' in the Psalms.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The 242 family heads and Amessai son of Esdriel are not identified with Chronicles' differently named Maasaia chain or larger priestly total; the candidate remains unresolved.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit gives 128 men strong for battle under the overseer Badiel; the other texts share only battle language and different numbers, and Badiel appears nowhere else.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The 128 men strong for battle and their overseer Badiel are not made identical to the different Chronicles priestly service total or an unverified similarly named overseer.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is the bare total of 284; the other texts mention the holy city or contain unrelated numbers, and none records this total.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The bare total of 284 belongs to its local Levitical context; no separately verified equal enumeration is established by the selected parallel register.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says only that the king's command was upon them; the other texts concern provisions for singers or Persian decrees for the temple, but none names this command, and the king here is unnamed.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The king is unnamed in this short command notice, so the command is not identified with a particular Davidic, Solomonic or Persian order merely because singers are in the surrounding context.

closed_source_units.reason: Pathaia son of Baseza, at the king's hand for the people, appears nowhere else; the other texts concern Zerah, David's officials or Levitical service and share only the word 'hand'.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Pathaia son of Baseza at the king's hand is not equated with a similarly named priest, Levite or official without a matching ancestry and role.

closed_source_units.reason: Jesou here is a town in the settlement list; the Joshua town lists shown contain no such name, and the other Jesou is a Levite, not a place.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Jesou in the settlement list has no securely established corresponding place in the inspected Joshua list; it is not silently normalized to a different city from another numbering tradition.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit notes that Levitical portions of Jouda were for Beniamin; the other texts concern Jacob's scattering of Levi, Jerusalem's Judahite and Benjaminite residents or offerings for Levites, none describing this allocation.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The short notice about Levitical portions of Jouda for Beniamin does not specify enough to identify a particular earlier Levitical land allocation or infer a transfer mechanism.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is only the fragment 'for the service divisions', continuing a list of Levites; other occurrences of service divisions or courses describe different arrangements, and the fragment itself names no group to match.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The fragment for the service divisions continues its local Levitical list; a generic occurrence of service divisions elsewhere does not identify this precise group or assignment.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit traces the high-priestly line Jodae, Jonathan, Jadou; the other texts concern a priest Jodae of an earlier list or Jodae the father of David's officer Banaias, different men.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The Jonathan/Jadou genealogy is not silently harmonized with Joanan/Idoua in the later registration notice; the candidate personal identities remain unresolved.

closed_source_units.reason: Arem, Adnas, Marioth and Elkai are priestly family heads; the only other text names a Marioth in the high priest's ancestry generations earlier, not this family head.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Arem, Adnas, Marioth and Elkai are kept as printed; resembling priestly course names do not securely identify the family heads or justify silently restoring absent earlier list units.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names the priestly houses Abia and Beniamin with their heads; the other texts concern the tribe or sons of Beniamin living in Jerusalem, not a priestly house, so they share only a name.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Abia's appearance in an earlier priestly lot list does not alone establish the same named family's institutional continuity here, and the other short phrases are not normalized from another edition; the candidate remains unresolved.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names the priestly houses Balga and Semeia with their heads Samoue and Jonathan; the only other text lists a singer Semeias at the wall dedication, a different person.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The Balga and Semeia family representatives have no independently established individual identities in the selected source material.

closed_source_units.reason: Joiarib, Maththanai, Idia and Ozi are priestly family heads; the other texts name different men called Ozi in high-priestly and Issacharite genealogies.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Joiarib, Maththanai, Idia and Ozi are not assigned identities in another priestly list merely by name resemblance and office.

closed_source_units.reason: Sallai, Kallai, Amouk and Abed are priestly family heads; the other texts concern Gaal son of Abed at Shechem, an unrelated man.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Sallai, Kallai, Amouk and Abed have no verified matching personal or family notice retained in this pass.

closed_source_units.reason: The priestly houses Elkia and Jedeiou with heads Asabias and Nathanael are not shown elsewhere; the other texts name a Levite Nathanael and Asabias under Josiah, an assistant of Esdras, and Elkia in the high priest's ancestry, all different men.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The Elkia and Jedeiou representatives are not equated with similarly named priests or ancestors from other generations without firmer evidence.

closed_source_units.reason: The fragment 'when I gathered the gatekeepers' records Nehemiah's own act; the other texts describe gatekeeper divisions or duties under David, Solomon or Jehoiada, or use 'gatekeepers' figuratively, none referring to this gathering.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The fragment about gathering the gatekeepers does not by itself establish a particular additional gathering event or identify the listed personnel elsewhere.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit explains that the singers had built farmsteads for themselves around Jerusalem; the other texts concern Benjaminite towns, Levitical cities, farmsteads of Judah's settlers or Egypt's plague, none describing the singers' settlements.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The singers' farmsteads explain where the local gathering came from; no separately verified matching farmstead settlement or ownership is established.

closed_source_units.reason: Osaia and half the rulers of Jouda appear only in this dedication procession. The Osaia of Ezra 8:19 is a Merarite Levite brought back with Ezra, not shown in any processional role, and the other passages only mention the rulers or sons of Jouda in general settlement lists. Nothing identifies this group elsewhere.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Osaia and half the rulers are a specific processional attendance notice without an independently verified matching group; they are not assumed to be the same half as the second procession's people.

closed_source_units.reason: Azarias, Esdras and Mesoulam are named only as members of this procession. Other texts with Azaria, Esdra(s) or Mesoulam involve different contexts: a covenant-sealing list, a priestly house headed by Mesoulam, the returnee leaders, Ezra's genealogy and a gate repairer. None shows these men in this role, and the names are too common to establish identity.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Azarias, Esdras and Mesoulam in the procession are not individually identified through their common names alone.

closed_source_units.reason: Jouda, Beniamin, Samaia and Jermia are processional participants. The other passages use Jouda and Beniamin as tribal names in settlement lists, not as these individuals, and no text shows the same Samaia or Jermia in this ceremony.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Jouda, Beniamin, Samaia and Jermia in the procession have no separately verified individual correspondence retained here.

closed_source_units.reason: The verse lists participants in the dedication and notes that the singers were heard. Similar names elsewhere (Ozi the Levite overseer, Maasia and Melchia in a genealogy, Eleazar and Melchia among the sons of Phoros, Joanan son of Karee) are not shown to be the same people. The praise psalms are only generic calls to shout for joy and do not touch this specific ceremony.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The named singers and their being heard and appointed are kept in their local ceremony; no identities are assigned from similar names in another music list.
